      "body": "GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a caller who only has the `view` scope on the all-groups resource is treated as having global group manage permission. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage(), meaning a view-only FGAP admin could create top-level groups. This should evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE for canManage()."

      "title": "getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs",
      "body": "In V2, individual group resources are looked up by name equal to the group id, but this method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. groupResource.getId() is the generated authorization resource UUID, not the group id, so hasPermission() usually cannot find the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The resulting set is then used as UserModel.GROUPS in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount, filtering users by IDs that are not actual group IDs. For example, an all-groups view-members permission can produce an invalid group id and return no users in search. It should use groupResource.getName() for both evaluation and grant collection."

      "title": "New group resources are created without a resource type",
      "body": "When getOrCreateResource() creates a missing resource for a resource type, it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). The all-resource entries created in init() do set a type, but per-group resources created later do not. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources, so group-specific resources with a null type are skipped. This makes the group-id set incomplete and causes user search pre-filtering and user counts based on group view-members permissions to be wrong."

This PR removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from both checks. A master realm admin with the admin role but without the target realm's manage-users/view-users management-client role can now be denied per-user operations. Unless AdminRoles.ADMIN is guaranteed to be a composite containing those target-realm roles, this is an authorization regression."

findings.title: VIEW all-groups permission grants global group manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so a caller who only has the `view` scope on the all-groups resource is treated as having global group manage permission. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage(), meaning a view-only FGAP admin could create top-level groups. This should evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE for canManage().

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In V2, individual group resources are looked up by name equal to the group id, but this method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. groupResource.getId() is the generated authorization resource UUID, not the group id, so hasPermission() usually cannot find the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The resulting set is then used as UserModel.GROUPS in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount, filtering users by IDs that are not actual group IDs. For example, an all-groups view-members permission can produce an invalid group id and return no users in search. It should use groupResource.getName() for both evaluation and grant collection.

findings.title: New group resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: When getOrCreateResource() creates a missing resource for a resource type, it never calls resource.setType(resourceType). The all-resource entries created in init() do set a type, but per-group resources created later do not. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources, so group-specific resources with a null type are skipped. This makes the group-id set incomplete and causes user search pre-filtering and user counts based on group view-members permissions to be wrong.

findings.title: AdminRoles.ADMIN is no longer accepted for per-user V2 evaluations
findings.body: canView(UserModel) at line 48 and canManage(UserModel) at line 57 previously granted access when the caller had AdminRoles.ADMIN, in addition to MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS. This PR removes AdminRoles.ADMIN from both checks. A master realm admin with the admin role but without the target realm's manage-users/view-users management-client role can now be denied per-user operations. Unless AdminRoles.ADMIN is guaranteed to be a composite containing those target-realm roles, this is an authorization regression.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel).
